item.title: NAIC readies AI Risk Evaluation Supplement v7.0 for Fall National Meeting adoption
item.description: The NAIC's Big Data and Artificial Intelligence (H) Working Group circulated draft version 7.0 of its AI Risk Evaluation Supplement, the optional exhibits market conduct and financial examiners use to ask insurers about their AI use, and plans to present it for adoption at the Fall National Meeting in Texas, November 14 to 17. The revision lets regulators exclude GLMs and other static, transparent predictive models from the Supplement altogether, adds guidance on judging 'human in the loop' controls for agentic AI, and pairs questions with documentation requests so examiners can corroborate insurers' answers. It follows more than 20 comment letters from trade associations, vendors and AI-governance consultants, according to law firm McDermott.

item.title: Accelerant's $4B Thoma Bravo sale puts specialty MGA capacity terms in focus
item.description: Atlanta-based Accelerant, which runs the Accelerant Risk Exchange connecting specialty MGAs with risk capital, reported third-quarter Exchange Written Premium of $1.33 billion, up 27% year over year, with third-party direct written premium reaching 49% of volume versus 32% a year earlier. The results land as Thoma Bravo's all-cash take-private deal, valued at more than $4 billion, heads toward an expected first-half 2027 close, and brokers placing business through MGAs on the exchange are watching whether the underlying capacity terms hold. Accelerant skipped its earnings call and is not issuing fourth-quarter or full-year guidance.

item.title: Ancep raises $8.5M for AI agents that help brokers place turned-away risks
item.description: Ancep, which builds AI agents for commercial insurance brokers, raised $8.5 million in a round led by Creandum, with Kleiner Perkins and Vicus Ventures participating alongside angel investors including a former Aon CFO and a former Marsh chairman. Its agents handle the routine stages of a placement: reading the client's submission, building the broker's standard documents and approaching insurers for terms by email, portal or API, all inside the policy admin systems, e-trade portals and CRMs brokers already run. The company said the funds will support growth and hiring.

item.title: StitchStudio raises $8M for auditable AI agents that work inside insurers' legacy systems
item.description: Oregon-based StitchStudio raised $8 million in a round led by Voyager Capital, with Lookout Ventures and Grit Capital Partners joining earlier backers ManchesterStory and BrokerTech Fund, following a $3 million seed round in 2025. Its AI agents connect to carriers' and brokers' existing systems rather than replacing them, with every action traceable and auditable, and handle tasks such as quote comparison, sales agent onboarding and billing checks for customers including M3 Insurance, Heffernan Insurance Brokers and Fidelity Life. The funding will go toward new products for employee benefits, life and annuities, and commercial property cover.

item.title: Optalitix adds agentic AI to its Quote pricing and underwriting platform
item.description: Pricing and underwriting insurtech Optalitix rolled out agentic AI in its Optalitix Quote platform, letting insurers, reinsurers and MGAs that build pricing in Excel and Python automate workflows such as reviewing claims history, spotting irregularities in loss data, assessing risk accumulation, checking quotes against authority limits and preparing renewals. The agents work on top of each insurer's existing models, rules and sign-off procedures, do not set prices on their own, and log every action in an auditable trail. Through the Model Context Protocol, clients can connect assistants such as ChatGPT, Claude and Copilot to live quote data, with a further phase planned for Q1 2027.

item.title: OutSystems launches Agentic First Notice of Loss for auto insurers
item.description: Boston-based OutSystems expanded its Agentic Industry Solutions portfolio into insurance with Agentic First Notice of Loss, a pre-built solution that connects AI agents, customer applications and existing claims systems to modernize auto claims reporting and intake. Coverage, liability and payment decisions stay with human adjusters. Through a strategic partnership with roadside assistance technology provider Honk, the solution can arrange a tow while the policyholder reports the loss, with its status and ETA visible in the insurer's app.

item.title: PremFina and boom partner on embedded premium finance for UK digital insurance
item.description: UK premium finance provider PremFina formed a long-term partnership with boom, the digital insurance brand operated by Abacai Technologies Limited, part of the Abacai group. Through a direct integration with PremFina's technology platform, boom customers will be able to spread the cost of their premiums in instalments within boom's own digital journey instead of paying the full amount upfront. boom said it selected PremFina after reviewing the market, citing its technology, service-based approach and ability to support a growing digital insurance business.
